xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5195: File explorer: discard untracked and newly added files to the Overdeck trash

plan.title: File explorer: discard untracked and newly added files to the Overdeck trash
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The file explorer's Discard changes action (pan.explorerGitStage, action 'discard') refuses any request that names a path not in HEAD, or a folder holding an index entry not in HEAD, with NOT_IMPLEMENTED, because a no-overlay git restore would delete such files. The operator cannot discard untracked or newly added files. PAN-5187 shipped trashPaths but nothing wires discard to it.
narratives.Proposal: Change gitStage discard to: resolve paths and read HEAD and index (failures throw before any change); unstage requested paths holding index entries not in HEAD with 'git restore --staged'; list what git then reports as untracked (--others --exclude-standard --directory, so an ignored file is never trashed on its own and a new folder is one entry); move those to the Overdeck trash with trashPaths; restore the requested paths that have HEAD content from HEAD. Return { trashIds } in a now-required ExplorerGitStageResult field so PAN-5190's undo can restore them, and make the frontend wrapper return the result. Update docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md and add changelog.d/pan-5195.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No undo or redo UI for discard (PAN-5190 owns undo and reads trashIds)
- No change to the discard confirm dialog or the context menu's enablement rules
- Discarding the new path of a staged rename does not restore the rename's original path; the original stays staged as deleted
- Discarding an untracked symlink whose target is outside the root, or a dangling one, stays refused with PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT
- Discard in a repository with no commits fails with EXPLORER_FAILED; no special path for an unborn HEAD
- No change to trashPaths, restore or pruneTrash in trash.ts
- Never trash an ignored file on its own or an unchanged committed file; an ignored file inside a wholly new untracked folder goes to the trash with that folder

autoDecisions.summary: A folder with committed and new files: trash only the new entries inside it and restore the committed files from HEAD
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's 'What is needed' already describes this split, and refusing would keep the reported bug for every mixed folder.

autoDecisions.summary: Return trash ids as a required trashIds field on ExplorerGitStageResult ([] for stage and unstage)
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-5190's undo needs the ids; the explorer is unreleased (changelog.d only), so no older server answers {} to a newer client.

autoDecisions.summary: The trash set is git's untracked listing after unstaging, never 'not in HEAD'
autoDecisions.rationale: The context menu sends every selected target; a multi-select holding an ignored .env must not trash it. An ignored file inside a wholly new folder still goes with that folder.

autoDecisions.summary: Unstage with 'git restore --staged' by pathspec before listing and trashing
autoDecisions.rationale: git rm --cached fails on a staged file edited after staging (probed); unstaging first collapses a partly staged new folder into one trash entry and loses no content if a later step fails.

autoDecisions.summary: A new folder containing ignored files is trashed whole
autoDecisions.rationale: git lists it as one collapsed untracked entry; the trash is recoverable and leaving only ignored files behind would not discard the folder.

metadata.acJustification: Six ACs: each pins one discard rule (mixed folder, collapsed new folder, ignored file, edited staged file, new folder with ignored contents, restore failure after trash) that could otherwise yield a different-but-plausible diff.

narrative.Action: the PAN-5195 PRD under .pan/drafts/ WI-2 and decisions D-1..D-9. In git.ts replace pathsNotInHead with discardPlan (ls-tree HEAD + ls-files reads; any non-zero, timedOut or truncated read throws EXPLORER_FAILED before changes; returns head = requested paths with HEAD content, unstage = requested paths with an index entry not in HEAD). Add untrackedEntries (ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard --directory --no-empty-directory -- paths, strip one trailing '/'). Discard order: unstage via 'git restore --staged -- <unstage>' (never git rm --cached: it fails on a staged file edited after staging), list untracked, trashPaths(root, untracked) when non-empty, then 'git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <head>' when non-empty; a restore failure after a trash throws EXPLORER_FAILED 'git restore failed: <why>; moved to the Overdeck trash: <ids>'. Return { trashIds }. Rewrite the header's last paragraph (D-9). In git.test.ts delete the two 'refuses to discard ...' cases and add a describe block whose beforeEach/afterEach isolate process.env.OVERDECK_HOME in a mkdtemp dir (trash.test.ts pattern), with the ten cases named in PRD WI-2 step 6 (the tenth creates .git/index.lock after setup so the HEAD restore fails after the trash).

items.title: Given a mixed folder dir with a modified committed dir/a.txt, a staged-new dir/new.txt and an untracked dir/sub/s.txt, when discard runs on ['dir'], then dir/a.txt is restored to its HEAD content, dir/new.txt and dir/sub no longer exist, and trashIds has length 2
Given a new folder nd with one staged file and one untracked file, when discard runs on ['nd'], then trashIds has exactly one id and nd no longer exists in the worktree
Given an ignored x.log selected next to a modified a.txt, when discard runs on ['a.txt','x.log'], then x.log still exists and the result is { trashIds: [] }
Given a staged-new file edited after staging, when discard runs on it, then git ls-files prints nothing for it and its content exists under <OVERDECK_HOME>/trash/<id>/files/
Given a new untracked folder newdir holding newdir/x and an ignored newdir/z.log, when discard runs on ['newdir'], then trashIds has length 1 and <OVERDECK_HOME>/trash/<id>/files/newdir/z.log exists

Given a modified committed d.txt, an untracked u.txt and an existing .git/index.lock, when discard runs on ['d.txt','u.txt'], then it rejects with EXPLORER_FAILED whose message contains 'moved to the Overdeck trash: issue-x/', and u.txt exists under <OVERDECK_HOME>/trash/ while d.txt keeps its modified content
Frontend gitStage wrapper returns the RPC result
